title: Why We Remember Ordinary Days
excerpt: The coffee, the walk home, the book someone left on the table. Sometimes the smallest moments become the ones we keep.
body:
Memory rarely arrives as a perfect photograph. More often, it returns as a smell, a street, a sentence, or the sound of someone laughing in another room.

That is part of what shaped Before You Forget Me: the belief that a life is held together by details we barely notice while they are happening.

The story lives in those details—quiet afternoons, old letters, books exchanged between people, and the strange way a place can hold a version of us long after we have left it.

title: The Shimla Behind the Story
excerpt: A note on the atmosphere behind the novel and why the hills became such an important part of its emotional world.
body:
Shimla gives the novel its sense of distance and memory. It is not simply a setting; it is a place where the past and present can feel close enough to touch.

The streets, old houses, lake light and changing seasons became part of the emotional language of the story.

Before You Forget Me moves through that atmosphere to ask a simple question: what happens when the place remembers, even when people do not?

title: A Note to the People Who Keep Letters
excerpt: For anyone who has ever kept a ticket, a photograph, a pressed flower, or a handwritten page because throwing it away felt impossible.
body:
There is something about a handwritten page that makes time feel physical. You can fold it, keep it inside a book, find it years later and suddenly remember who you were when it was written.

Letters became an important thread in Before You Forget Me because they allow the past to speak without pretending that the past can be changed.

If you keep old letters, you probably understand the feeling. If you do not, perhaps this story will make you want to start.
